Re-Elect Laura Hoffmeister
# Experienced Leadership for Concord
Focused on what matters now: repairing our streets, keeping neighborhoods safe, maintaining safe, clean parks and playgrounds
## Priorities
#### Repairing our streets
I've kept road conditions front and center. Concord has a steady repaving program underway on Clayton Road, Treat Boulevard, Willow Pass Road and Concord Boulevard, with more residential paving to come. I'm also backing interconnected traffic signals to keep traffic moving.
#### Keeping neighborhoods safe
Recruiting and retaining qualified staff is a top priority. Our police chief reports sworn positions are fully staffed, with additional trainees in the academy. Concord also opened its Real Time Intelligence Center to help officers respond to and solve crimes with better information.
#### Safe, clean parks and playgrounds
I supported improvements at Newhall Community Park to improve water quality and restore habitat, and I've backed the events that make Todos Santos Plaza Concord’s outdoor living room.
#### Senior and youth programs
I've supported senior mobility through Concord Go! and GoGo Concord, and youth camps, swim lessons and a Youth Scholarship Program that helps income-eligible kids take part.
#### Real progress on homelessness
Concord is making measurable progress on homelessness. The unsheltered count fell from 241 in 2023 to 91 in 2026. I've backed a dedicated CORE outreach team and partnerships with organizations like Hope Solutions on rapid rehousing and housing support.

- Helped select Brookfield as the master developer to guide the responsible reuse of the former Concord Naval Weapons Station with the community.
- Worked to secure a 100-yard buffer between any new development and existing homes, a direct response to residents who asked that their neighborhoods be protected.
- Ensured roughly 2,500 acres will become a new East Bay Regional Park District park, open to all residents.
- Supported new affordable housing downtown near BART, including Blue Oak Square (181 all-affordable apartments in the heart of Concord) and roughly 400 units of now-occupied downtown housing for seniors, veterans, people with disabilities and other residents.
- Backed Concord's First-Time Homebuyer Program, which offers down-payment assistance to help local families become homeowners.

- Worked to maintain balanced budgets and a Rainy Day Fund that helped Concord weather pandemic-related economic uncertainty.
- Voted to place Measure O on this fall’s ballot to modernize Concord's nearly 40-year-old business-license tax, replacing an outdated structure in which smaller businesses paid a higher rate than larger ones with a simpler, fairer system, and generating locally controlled funding for core services like road maintenance and emergency response.
Show Less
## EXPERIENCE THAT DELIVERS
My parents came to the Bay Area looking for opportunity, fell in love with this corner of California and raised me here in Concord. It's where I grew up, where my friends and my family are, where my mother still lives. It's the community I've devoted my life to serving.
I've watched Concord grow and change over the decades, through good times and hard ones, and that long view is exactly what I bring to the council. I know this city because it's home.
There's more to do — and I'll keep at it. I want the very best for Concord and my neighbors. I'd be honored to have your vote.
#### Public service record
- Mayor of Concord in 2023, 2017, 2016, 2011, 2009, 2005 and 2001
- Vice Mayor in 2022, 2015, 2010, 2008, 2004 and 2000
- Chair of the Local Reuse Authority, overseeing the Concord Naval Weapons Station reuse, in 2023, 2016, 2011, 2009 and 2005
- Current member of the City Council's Infrastructure & Franchise and Youth & Education committees
- Helped found the Bicycle Pedestrian Advisory Task Force, which established Concord's first permanent Bicycle Pedestrian Advisory Committee
- Contra Costa Mayors Conference: Chair in 2019, Vice Chair in 2018 and a member of its Executive Committee from 2015 to 2020 and from 2000 to 2004
- County Connection Board of Directors: current Vice Chair, past Chair in 2017 and 2008 and a member since 1998; past Chair of its Administration and Finance Committee
- 2026 Chair of the Contra Costa County Countywide Oversight Board, which oversees the wind-down of the county's former redevelopment agencies
- Member of the Contra Costa County Airport Land Use Commission since 2026
- Member of the League of California Cities, East Bay Division
- Board member of the John Muir Community Health Fund
#### Honors and community
- Recipient of the Contra Costa Women's Hall of Fame Award for Community Leadership (2002)
- Rotary Paul Harris Fellow
- Save Mount Diablo Mountain Star Leadership Award (2024)
- Graduate of the Community Emergency Response Team (CERT) program
- Active supporter of veterans and veterans' organizations, including VFW Post 1525-Clayton Valley and Diablo Valley Veterans
- Life member and former board member of the Concord Historical Society
#### Before the City Council
Before her election, Laura was an active member of the Greater Concord Chamber of Commerce and the Concord Ambassadors, and a graduate of the Chamber's Leadership Concord program. She holds a bachelor's degree in city and environmental planning from UC Davis, with a minor in environmental geology.
